A frozen feed-forward geometry encoder extracts cross-view representations from monocular RGB history, and a trainable 3D Scene-to-Token Adapter converts them into a fixed-length scene prefix for the world-action Diffusion Transformer. Through block-causal attention, this prefix remains visible to every future video-action block throughout joint denoising, providing persistent geometric context. We train WNM-3D with supervised world-action learning, DAgger-style adaptation on policy-visited states, and Counterfactual DanceGRPO refinement. Across GN-Bench and VLN-CE, WNM-3D consistently outperforms the backbone-matched WNM-2D counterpart, demonstrating gains from 3D scene conditioning across distinct visual domains. WNM-3D further outperforms strong VLN baselines on GN-Bench and demonstrates closed-loop deployment on a physical robot. Component and stage-wise ablations support the Adapter design and the complementary roles of DAgger-SFT and subsequent reward-guided refinement.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: The No-Meaning Falsity: The Structural Impossibility of the Arbitrary Sign in Classical Arabic
nodes.authors: Elnaserledinellah Mahmoud Abdelwahab
nodes.summary: This paper investigates whether the postmodern claim of unrestricted semantic indeterminacy, and its foundational Saussurean axiom of the arbitrary sign, are compatible with the structural architecture of Classical Arabic. We develop a formal mathematical model of Arabic non concatenative morphology in which lexical meaning is determined by the interaction between an invariant root and a morphosyntactic pattern. Within this framework, we establish a Morphological Correspondence Theorem, demonstrating that every lexical item is uniquely generated by a root pattern pair, and a Semantic Localization Theorem, proving that lexical meaning is determined at the derivational level prior to surface realization. To address Saussurean weaker notion of relative arbitrariness, we formalize it via conditional Kolmogorov complexity, defining arbitrariness algorithmically as the no rule property. We prove that general relative arbitrariness is formally undecidable, while Arabic relative arbitrariness is decidable and provably less than 1 for its motivated signifiers (Levels W and M), establishing a strict system complexity asymmetry over Indo-European languages.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: HazeSpikeMamba: Coupling Spiking-Inspired and State-Space Features for Self-Supervised Real-World Dehazing
nodes.authors: Haoran Liu, Li Xu, Mingzhe Liu, Huibin Li, Peng Li, Guibin Zan, Simon X. Yang
nodes.summary: Dehazing networks are commonly trained on synthetic hazy-clear pairs, but their performance often drops on real photographs. Synthetic haze generated using the atmospheric scattering model does not fully capture the variability of real haze, and paired real hazy-clear images are scarce. In this work, we propose HazeSpikeMamba, a compact dehazing framework that combines a spiking-inspired local path and an attentive state-space global path in a multi-scale U-Net. The local path uses TPCNNSpike, a new spike-emission scheme inspired by the neighborhood coupling of Pulse-Coupled Neural Network (PCNN). Unlike grouped directional scanning, TPCNNSpike updates all neurons in parallel using the previous firing states of their Gaussian-weighted neighborhoods. The global path adapts the Attentive State-Space Module of MambaIRv2, retaining semantic prompting and sequence reordering while removing the window self-attention branch. Its state-space processing models long-range dependencies with complexity linear in sequence length. For target-domain adaptation, a frozen degradation network, pretrained on paired NH-HAZE data, re-synthesizes haze from the dehazed prediction. The reconstruction error updates only the final restoration layers of HazeSpikeMamba without haze-free labels during adaptation. A shared checkpoint is adapted once on each complete unlabeled target set, making the evaluation dataset-level and transductive rather than zero-shot or per-image optimization. The forward network contains 2.02M active parameters and requires 13.27G nominal MACs (measured with thop at 256x256 input). This adaptation consistently improves BRISQUE and NIMA on RTTS, URHI, and HSTS. On RTTS, BRISQUE decreases from 30.13 to 27.72 and NIMA increases from 4.13 to 4.87. Under this transductive protocol, the adapted model also achieves the best BRISQUE and NIMA on URHI and HSTS among the compared methods.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: TEMPO: Semantic-Action Decoupled RL Post-Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
nodes.authors: Ziheng Liu, Quantao Yang
nodes.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are commonly adapted to downstream manipulation tasks via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or online reinforcement learning(RL) post-training. SFT is prone to distribution mismatch, and existing RL approaches typically optimize all trainable components within a single RL loop at a uniform update rate, although these components play distinct functional roles. We propose TEMPO, a semantic-action decoupled, two-timescale RL post-training framework for VLA models. TEMPO freezes the pretrained vision-language backbone and adapts two components with dedicated RL loops: the semantic projection layer, which produces the latent action conditioning the action expert, and the low-level action expert itself. The semantic projection layer is updated infrequently and the action expert frequently, which aims to limit latent-action drift while allowing the action expert to learn from online feedback. Our analyses show that, compared with equal update frequencies, less frequent semantic updates reduce latent-action drift and improve policy performance. Experiments on the CALVIN benchmark and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that TEMPO outperforms both pretrained state-of-the-art VLA models and the RL post-training baseline, while reaching and maintaining higher evaluation rewards on three real-world tasks.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Addressable Memory for Video World Models
nodes.authors: Xindi Wu, Sven Elflein, James Lucas, Olga Russakovsky, Laura Leal-Taixé, Despoina Paschalidou, Jonathan Lorraine, Aljoša Ošep
nodes.summary: We study visual persistence in interactive video world models. These models rely on a Key-Value (KV) cache as a growing visual memory to carry forward previously generated frames. However, we find that models can no longer reliably address stored content once rollouts extend beyond the training horizon, because temporal Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE) offsets can exceed the training range and the model struggles to retrieve the relevant visual information through attention. Moreover, naively compressing the cache in the RoPE-rotated space degrades memory by averaging keys with incompatible positional phases. To address this, we propose WorldTrace, a training-free memory framework for long-horizon visual persistence. WorldTrace keeps compressed memory addressable by assigning each summary slot a distinct, in-distribution virtual position. Within this cache, WorldTrace uses the model's own attention to decide which observations to retain verbatim and which redundant ones to merge into compressed summaries, all within one bounded addressable memory bank. We evaluate this ability with LoopBench, a benchmark that tests whether a compressed cache can reconstruct a previously visited scene after a long detour. On LoopBench, WorldTrace improves average DINOv2 recall similarity by 32.6% over a sliding window at the same cache budget, extending visually persistent generation without retraining.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: What Should Visual Place Recognition Be Invariant To? Rethinking Condition Invariance in Visual Place Recognition
nodes.authors: Beomsu Kim, Minwoo Jung, Giseop Kim
nodes.summary: Condition invariance in Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is typically evaluated by matching queries from one condition against a database from another condition. This tests the ability to recognize the same place when the query's condition differs from the database's condition. However, to map large environments, a database can be built from images collected by multiple robots or across multiple traversals under different conditions. In this setting, condition blindness---the ability to remain invariant to condition differences among database images---becomes important, but standard cross-condition evaluation does not provide a controlled assessment of this ability. Therefore, we introduce Distractor-Augmented Recall (DAR) to measure condition blindness in a controlled manner. Across eleven methods and six datasets, we find that differences in condition blindness can be larger than Recall@1 alone would suggest. To improve the condition blindness that DAR reveals, we compare three methods that make VPR descriptors more invariant to condition changes through post-processing. Among the three methods, we demonstrate INLP on a database built from multiple traversals under different conditions, showing that it can improve the performance of existing VPR methods.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: LC-GRPO: Bridging Train-Inference Gap for Flow-Based GRPO with Langevin Correction
nodes.authors: Yingqing Guo, Hui Yuan, Zijian He, Mengdi Wang, Zheng Ding
nodes.summary: Flow-based generative models are typically sampled by solving a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE), whereas reinforcement learning (RL) requires stochastic rollouts for exploration and optimization. Existing online RL methods for flow models therefore replace the inference-time ODE with a stochastic differential equation (SDE) during training. Although the ODE and SDE share the same marginal distribution in continuous time, they can behave differently after finite-step discretization. In particular, SDE rollouts often become blurry as exploration noise increases, creating a mismatch between training rollouts and inference-time ODE samples. We introduce LC-GRPO, a flow-based GRPO framework with Langevin correction. Each rollout transition takes an inference-aligned ODE Euler step followed by a stochastic Langevin correction targeting the marginal at the resulting timestep. The required score is recovered directly from the flow velocity, requiring no additional score model, while the transition remains an isotropic Gaussian with tractable likelihood. We theoretically show that, under suitable conditions, a single Langevin correction step reduces the error of an imperfect ODE Euler step and, under matched randomness, yields a more accurate transition than standard Euler--Maruyama discretization of the reverse SDE. Additionally, experiments on SD3.5-Medium, FLUX.1-Dev, and HunyuanVideo show that LC-GRPO consistently improves reward optimization across text-to-image and text-to-video tasks, preserves generation quality, and substantially narrows the gap between stochastic training rollouts and deterministic ODE inference.
nodes.subject: Gaussian Splatting

nodes.title: Vorch-Director: Interactive World Story Model via Noise-Aware Error Rectification
nodes.authors: Lisai Zhang, Yidi Wu, Qi Liu, Xin Ma, Yang Ding, Gang Yue, Siqian Yang, Jingyuan Chen, Lin Ma, Yaohui Wang
nodes.summary: Autoregressive continuation provides a natural path toward minute-scale audio-visual generation by repeatedly extending a short-window generator conditioned on previously generated video and audio. However, models are trained on clean ground-truth histories, while inference relies on their own generated histories, where accumulated errors cause identity drift, over-smoothing, and audio-visual desynchronization. Recent methods reduce this mismatch by reusing prediction residuals as synthetic corruption, but we observe that the effectiveness of residual correction critically depends on the flow-matching noise level at which residuals are produced. We propose Vorch-Director, a noise-level-aware residual correction strategy that associates each residual with its originating noise level and injects residuals from matched noise regimes during training. By aligning injected errors with the denoising process, Vorch-Director produces more realistic autoregressive histories while retaining efficient teacher-forcing training. Built on the audio-visual LTX-2 diffusion transformer, Vorch-Director further introduces task embeddings to distinguish historical video, reference images, and target video, enabling unified conditioning for long-horizon generation. Together with a clean conditioning sink and mixed-task training, Vorch-Director supports multi-shot, multi-subject, reference-guided audio-visual long-video generation. We evaluate Vorch-Director on ST-Bench and introduce a new long-horizon audio-visual benchmark with metrics for quality drift and long-range consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved stability and audio-visual fidelity over strong baselines.
nodes.subject: Video World Models

nodes.title: Adaptive-WAM: Quality-Guided Early-Exit Planning from Intermediate Video-Diffusion Features
nodes.authors: Sining Ang, Yuguang Yang, Yan Wang
nodes.summary: Large video diffusion models provide rich spatiotemporal priors for autonomous driving, but existing world-action models often inherit the cost of iterative future-video generation even though deployment only requires an ego trajectory. We ask a more basic question: how much of a video diffusion model must be executed to make a reliable driving decision? Through a controlled study of video denoising timesteps and Diffusion Transformer (DiT) depth, we find that planning performance is largely insensitive to the tested video-noise levels, whereas strong trajectories can already be decoded from intermediate layers. Based on this observation, we introduce Adaptive-WAM, a quality-aware multi-exit planner built on a Wan2.2-5B backbone. Trajectory diffusion heads are attached to selected DiT blocks, and a lightweight trajectory-quality scorer terminates inference once the best trajectory decoded so far satisfies a quality threshold; otherwise, computation continues from the cached hidden state to a deeper exit. The deployed planner therefore avoids the iterative classifier-free denoising loop and VAE decoding required for future-video synthesis, while dynamically allocating backbone depth according to trajectory quality. On NAVSIM, the adaptive single-trajectory planner achieves 90.8 PDMS; a separate fixed-exit variant reaches 92.6 PDMS with 64 proposals. It further obtains 89.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, yielding the best reported results among the compared front-view video world-model planners. Without target-domain fine-tuning, Adaptive-WAM transfers to nuScenes with 0.88 m average L2 error and a 0.08\% collision rate. On an A100, adaptive routing improves PDMS from 90.62 to 90.79 while averaging 170 ms end-to-end planning latency, approximately 10\% below the 190 ms fixed block-15 planner and 47\% below the 320 ms fixed full-depth planner. Code will be released.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: From Siloed Algorithms to Compliance-First Agentic Platforms: A Multi-Layered Architecture for Hospital AI Systems
nodes.authors: Manideep Dhar, Ritwik Singh, Sharat Chandra Kumar Manikonda
nodes.summary: Hospitals are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence for triage, imaging, scheduling etc., yet most deployments remain isolated point solutions locked inside departmental silos, resulting in duplicated effort, hidden risks, and unrealized enterprise value. Despite explosive growth of AI in healthcare market and accelerating investment, an estimated 70-80% of healthcare AI pilots fail to scale, largely due to governance gaps, fragmented data, and missing integration blueprints. This research proposes a hospital-specific, compliance-first, Agentic AI architecture with multiple interoperable layers, extending existing hospital AI platform models with: (i) an Agent Orchestration Layer for multi-agent workflows across clinical, operational, and financial domains, (ii) a Compliance and Policy Layer that centralizes policy-as-code for HIPAA, GDPR, the EU AI Act, DISHA Act, India's DPDP Act, and ISO/IEC security and safety standards, and (iii) a Privacy-Preserving Data Fabric that plugs federated learning, differential privacy, and secure enclaves into real-world Hospital Information Management System (HIMS) flows. Using a synthetic but structurally realistic hospital dataset and an open, ready-to-deploy prototype implementation, this study demonstrates the end-to-end orchestration of triage risk prediction, workflow optimization, and compliance logging, achieving substantial simulated reductions in task turnaround times and manual documentation effort while maintaining policy-guarded data access. The resulting architecture offers hospital leaders a pragmatic blueprint to move from ad hoc tools to a governed, globally compliant, ROI-focused AI platform that can be tailored to on-premise, hybrid and cloud-native deployments.
nodes.subject: Foundation Models

nodes.title: Scaling Inherently Interpretable Language Models
nodes.authors: GuideLabs, Andreas Madsen, Aya Abdelsalam Ismail, Giang Nguyen, Isaac Plant, Muawiz Chaudhary, Nathaniel Monson, Saqib Azim, Zhichen Guo, Julius Adebayo
nodes.summary:
Interpretability is often treated as a tax on capability: language models are trained as opaque systems, then explained after the fact, with methods whose reliability is difficult to establish. In this work, we challenge this premise. Rather than reverse-engineering a model, we make interpretability a constraint of the training pipeline, optimized alongside the language modeling objective. Across three orders of magnitude of compute, on both autoregressive and diffusion language models, interpretability scales with capability rather than against it. Surprisingly, model representations become more disentangled and aligned with human-understandable concepts with scale.
  We instantiate the training-time recipe with Steerling-8B, a diffusion language model with a causal attention mask. For any group of generated tokens, Steerling-8B attributes the output to relevant input tokens, human-understandable concepts, and training data. This enables closed-loop intervention: diagnose an output through its concept or feature attribution, retrieve similar training data, and correct the behavior through concept steering without retraining. Steerling-8B remains competitive with open peer models trained on substantially 2-16x more compute, suggesting a different scaling paradigm: interpretability can be designed into training, and it improves with scale.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: omni-macos: On-Device Omni-Modal Search on Apple Silicon
nodes.authors: Han Xiao
nodes.summary: We present omni-macos, a search engine that embeds text, code, documents, images, audio and video into one representation space and runs on the Mac that already holds the files, so the files, the queries and the vectors stay on that machine. A background indexer and an interactive search box share the device. Each distinct chunk is embedded and stored once, and every file becomes searchable from a small first share of its content. Indexer work is split into smaller units while the user types, and one memory setting reaches every allocator found to draw on unified memory. Once the index is large, queries scan a one-bit replica of it, rescore a shortlist exactly and rank every modality in one list on a common score scale. The engine can also leave the GPU entirely, with the encoder on the Neural Engine and search on the CPU. We measure omni-macos on five Macs spanning an eightfold range of accelerator width and a thirty-twofold range of memory, and its ranking on a labeled multilingual and multimodal testbed. omni-macos is open source under Apache 2.0 at https://github.com/hanxiao/omni-macos.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: ALTER: Modeling Longitudinal Changes via Regional Differencing for 3D CT Report Generation
nodes.authors: Dongchen Li, Jitao Liang, Wei Li
nodes.summary: Computed tomography (CT) is widely used for clinical diagnosis and longitudinal follow-up, yet automatically generating accurate and complete radiology reports from three-dimensional (3D) CT remains challenging. Existing methods improve fine-grained correspondence between images and text by modeling anatomical regions, but remain centered on the current examination. Consequently, patient-specific longitudinal changes within individual regions remain insufficiently modeled. Meanwhile, interval changes are often distributed across multiple anatomical regions, complicating a coherent assessment of the overall longitudinal state. We propose Anatomically Localized Temporal Evidence Representation (ALTER) to address these limitations. Global Prior Integration (GPI) incorporates the prior CT and report to establish historical context for the current examination. Regional Proxy Differencing (RPD) enables each current anatomical region to retrieve a historical proxy from a single shared encoding of the prior volume and to derive localized interval evidence. Interval Change Fusion (ICF) further combines current abnormality states with region-distributed differences, converting their joint representation into change-aware soft prompts that guide report generation. ALTER achieves state-of-the-art results on most evaluation metrics across the RadGenome-ChestCT validation and CTRG-Chest-548K test sets. Code and data preprocessing details are available at https://github.com/peytonkarlie/ALTER/tree/main.
nodes.subject: Gaussian Avatar

nodes.title: Breadcrumbing Search Agents: Per-Turn Scheming Over Long-Horizon Trajectories
nodes.authors: Xuebin Li, Hanqing Zhao, Siyuan Liang, Kejiang Chen, Weiming Zhang, Dacheng Tao, Nenghai Yu
nodes.summary: LLM-based search agents are widely used for information-seeking tasks, but their reliance on external tool returns introduces a critical security risk: web content retrieved during execution is untrusted, exposing agents to prompt injection and goal hijacking. Prior work on search-agent safety primarily focuses on static web-content injection, but modern agents issue follow-up queries and cross-check competing sources, so a single injected page is often diluted or rejected. We show that the channel delivering search and page observations is a fragile security boundary: beyond exposing the agent to a single poisoned page, a mediated search interface can repeatedly steer how the agent gathers evidence and forms its final answer. Under a constrained tool-intermediary threat model, appending only one controlled result per query can substantially increase attack success when the evidence is coordinated across the agent's trajectory. We study this setting with a strategy-driven long-horizon attack system and introduce Authority-Chain Hijack (ACH), an expert-refined strategy that turns isolated search-result and page-content manipulations into a coherent evidence chain across seemingly corroborating sources. ACH achieves the highest Overall ASR among all baselines, reaching 55.9% / 83.3% ASR / MaxN ASR on the full SafeSearch test split. We further introduce Trace-Guided Strategy Evolution (TGSE), which automatically improves attacker strategies from execution traces, replacing manual redesign with trace-driven refinement; its strongest single setting reaches 71.4% / 95.0% in held-out evaluation. Code is available at https://github.com/MBOSSLESS/Breadcrumbing-Search-Agents.
nodes.subject: Embodied Intelligence

nodes.title: Robust Context-Aware Detection of Malicious Instructions in Text
nodes.authors: Buzhao Liu, Xinhang Ma, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik
nodes.summary: The remarkable instruction-following ability of modern LLMs has enabled their practical use in orchestrating workflows of tool-using agents. This, however, also exposes such agents to attacks which embed malicious instructions in text, such as indirect prompt injection (IPI). One class of approaches to defend against such attacks aims to detect malicious sentences within otherwise benign text. While a number of approaches for this have been proposed, all tend to be brittle under adaptive paraphrasing attacks, in part because they do not capture sufficient global context to effectively differentiate malicious text from benign. We address this gap by developing an approach for malicious sentence classification that is both context- and query-aware, which we then harden against paraphrasing through two adversarial training (AT) methods: feature-space robust learning and AT with simulated LLM-based paraphrasing. Moreover, we parametrize the AT variants to facilitate a smooth tradeoff between utility and attack robustness. In extensive experiments using IPI benchmarks we show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art defense baselines under both static and adaptive paraphrasing attacks while preserving high utility. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/tavia-liu/CAD.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Retrieve in Time, Correct in Frequency
nodes.authors: Yuze Fan, Yue Cao, Pengjie Gao, Haojia Gao, Guangqiu Guo, Ziyue Zhang, Junbo Tan, Bokui Chen, Zhuo Zou, Xueqian Wang
nodes.summary: Frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policies generate temporally extended action chunks, but long-horizon manipulation remains vulnerable to accumulated execution error and visual aliasing across task stages. Successful rollouts provide useful corrective evidence, yet current frame retrieval can return progress-misaligned actions,while direct replay or time-domain fusion can overwrite the reactive structure of the policy proposal. We introduce Retrieve in Time, Correct in Frequency (RTCF), a training-free test-time correction framework that improves frozen VLA performance with low model-side overhead.RTCF separates which experience to retrieve from which part of its action to transfer. Progressive Memory Alignment (PMA) causally aligns the growing visual execution history with complete successful trajectories through incrementally updated monotonic frontiers, jointly identifying a relevant memory and the current aligned memory position without stage labels. From the aligned action chunk,RTCF transfers a coefficient-wise-clipped low-frequency residual on motion channels. Higher-frequency components and gripper decisions remain inherited from the frozen policy. Across four LIBERO suites and 2,000 episodes per condition, RTCF raises aggregate success from 86.4% to 88.4% and improves LIBERO-Long from 61.6% to 68.6%.These gains require no parameter updates, repeated VLA inference, or additional GPU resources: correction can be performed on the client CPU after a single policy invocation, and the median latencies sum to only 10.99 ms per action chunk
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Beyond Visibility: Real-Time Surface Accessibility Fields from Sparse LiDAR
nodes.authors: Bradley Scott, Sam Schofield, Richard Green
nodes.summary: Understanding which surfaces a given tool can physically access is fundamental to robotic interaction, yet 3D perception typically stops at geometric reconstruction or visibility estimation. Visibility does not imply accessibility: a visible point may still be blocked by tool geometry or approach-corridor clearance. We propose the Accessibility Field: a per-point surface accessibility labelling, computed from streaming sparse LiDAR and updated at sensor rate as the platform moves. Our GPU-based method evaluates surface points against precomputed tool-geometry kernels across rotated approach orientations, underpinned by a scan-centric TSDF integration scheme suited to non-repetitive sensors such as the Livox Mid-360. The system is tool-agnostic, requires no prior scene model, and runs in real time on both workstation and Jetson Orin edge hardware. On synthetic primitives, our method achieves F1=90.8%, against 69.8% for a Hidden Point Removal baseline; ablations within our own pipeline give 81.5% replacing the TSDF query with a point-cloud collision check, and 33.9% replacing scan-centric integration with projective, nvblox-style integration. On a mature synthetic Pinus radiata model, the method labels 56.8% of visible pine branch surfaces as physically inaccessible.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: The Judge is Part of the Experiment: Auditing Peer Context Sensitivity in LLM-Based Evaluation
nodes.authors: Alicia Guerra, Jiaming Qu, Yibo Hu
nodes.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based judges are increasingly used to evaluate AI systems. An underexplored area is applying these judges to multi-agent systems, where they may see the interactions behind a final answer. These interactions, which we call peer context, can affect an evaluation in two ways: (1) they can change the answer produced by the multi-agent system, because an agent might be swayed by other agents, and (2) they can change how a judge evaluates that same answer, depending on whether the judge sees them. In this paper, we separate these two effects through a controlled experiment. We first let an agent answer a question and then answer again after seeing peer responses. We then prompt judges to rate the same final answer with and without the peer context. Finally, we check whether the judges' ratings establish a valid measure of answer quality. Across three benchmarks, four open-weight LLMs as agents, and six judges, we find that peer context changes not only the answer but also how an identical answer is judged, and judges react to it in opposite directions. Moreover, providing peer context for a wrong answer misleads agents more than correct peers help them; without the correct answer, judges struggle to tell known-correct from known-wrong answers---a problem that a well-fitted statistical model does not reveal. Our results show that even when evaluating the same answer, how a judge is set up can change the conclusions differently. We therefore call for evaluations to report what each judge sees, document detailed results per judge, and validate rating scales. These practices are an important step toward the accountable use of LLM-based judges.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Eigenius: A Typed Knowledge-Graph DBMS with Epistemic Stratification and Institution-Mediated Reasoning
nodes.authors: Hans-Martin Will, Allen L. Brown, Matthew Fuchs
nodes.summary: As "AI Scientists" emerge to drive research via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), systems relying on ephemeral scripts will fail. The sheer scale of stateful, interconnected evidence requires a machine-walkable warranty grounded in a purpose-built database architecture. Eigenius is an open-source, typed knowledge-graph DBMS built on a single premise: answering the audit question ("what do you know, and what is your warranty?") requires a unified kernel. By tightly coupling the type system, storage engine, and integration protocol, Eigenius turns data provenance into a structural invariant rather than a property reconstructed across subsystem boundaries. The kernel rests on three pillars whose metatheory is mechanized in Lean 4: a dependent type theory (EigenTT) separating confluent conversion from ontology subsumption and keeping proof irrelevance axiomatic so distinct warrants remain inspectable; proof-calculus institutions acting as strongly typed integration boundaries; and a content-addressed immutable storage layer. Epistemic status (declared/observed/derived/verified) forms a bounded lattice over a justification logic enforced at commit. Cross-system comorphisms carry explicit axiom policies (Adopt, Discharge, Relativize), transport witnesses at commit, and materialize outputs into the graph, while EigenQL provides a Grothendieck query view across all hosted logics and shared on-chain IRs collapse multi-system translations to identity. Pairing empirical justification logic with an in-process Lean 4 term checker, an end-to-end recomputation of a published Nature study from pinned data discharges all 52 derived conclusions and surfaces four machine-checked discrepancies in the original study.
nodes.subject: Generative Recommendation Systems

nodes.title: OmniEdit-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Instruction-based Video Editing
nodes.authors: Chenxuan Miao, Yutong Feng, Yi Lu, Yunfeng Yan, Donglian Qi, Shiwei Zhang, Yu Liu, Xi Chen, Hengshuang Zhao
nodes.summary: Instruction-based video editing (IVE) offers diverse applications, yet evaluating editing models remains challenging. Existing benchmarks suffer from two key limitations: narrow task coverage inherited from image editing that overlooks video-specific dimensions, and metrics that inadequately capture instruction fidelity, allowing visually plausible but incorrect edits to receive high scores. To address these limitations, we introduce OmniEdit-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark covering spatial, temporal, audio, and reference-based editing. It distinguishes between explicit and implicit instructions and incorporates reasoning-based scenarios to reflect real-world editing requirements. We further propose an evaluation framework that assesses accuracy, preservation, realism, and consistency using both human judges and a state-of-the-art vision-language model (VLM). An accuracy-aware penalty mechanism conditions the other three scores on accuracy, prioritizing instruction fidelity and penalizing plausible but incorrect edits. Experiments on prominent open-source and commercial IVE models reveal substantial room for improvement. OmniEdit-Bench provides a structured testbed for identifying model limitations and advancing instruction-based video editing. Project page: https://omniedit-bench.github.io.
nodes.subject: Video World Models

nodes.title: MAGIC-SSCIL: Manifold Anchoring and Geometric Incremental Calibration for Semi-Supervised Class Incremental Learning
nodes.authors: Yousef Abdi, Mohammad Asadpour, Yousef Seyfari
nodes.summary: Exemplar-free semi-supervised class-incremental learning (SSCIL) asks a model to learn new classes from a few labeled and many unlabeled images without storing past data. A common recipe replays old classes from stored Gaussian statistics and pseudo-labels unlabeled data with a confidence threshold. With one or two labels per class, however, the model's confidence is a poor guide to which pseudo-labels are right, so the statistics that replay depends on rest on few or noisy samples. We propose MAGIC (Manifold Anchoring and Geometric Incremental Calibration), which propagates labels over a k-nearest-neighbor graph of frozen features and uses the propagated confidences as weights in the unlabeled loss and, through Soft-Weighted Geometry Calibration (SWGC), in the class statistics from which phantom features replay old classes. With a frozen ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and ImageNet-R at 1%, 5%, and 10% labels, we compare MAGIC with nine supervised class-incremental methods equipped with FixMatch and two native SSCIL methods. MAGIC gains from unlabeled data in all nine settings, most at 1%, and leads on fine-grained CUB-200 at every ratio; at 1% it is level with the best on ImageNet-R and 2.2 points behind the native SSCIL method TACLE on CIFAR-100. Experiments inside MAGIC show that most of this gain flows through the weighted statistics, not the loss, that at 1% labels graph pseudo-labels are more accurate than the model's own at equal coverage, and that a fixed threshold of 0.95 removes most of the gain. At higher ratios, baselines that adapt the backbone or model full covariances overtake MAGIC on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-R.
nodes.subject: Gaussian Splatting

nodes.title: Principles of Robot Autonomy
nodes.authors: Daniele Gammelli, Joseph Lorenzetti, Katie Luo, Gioele Zardini, Marco Pavone
nodes.summary: Autonomous robots are moving rapidly from research labs into everyday life - on roads, in the air, in warehouses, and in space. Robot autonomy is no longer solely an academic pursuit, but a collection of mature, field-tested methods and tools that practitioners rely on in real-world deployments. This book offers a clear, unified introduction to the methods that make this possible. Built on decades of teaching at Stanford, the text develops the core elements of modern autonomy stacks within a single conceptual framework, bridging classical robotics and modern physical AI. Every major topic is paired with hands-on Jupyter notebooks and implementation-driven exercises, so readers build practical intuition alongside theoretical understanding. The result is a principled, accessible, and deployment-aware foundation for anyone seeking to design, analyze, or contribute to the next generation of autonomous systems. This is a comprehensive resource for students, engineers, and researchers entering one of today's fastest-growing fields.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Shooting for Contact: Contact-Implicit Multiple Shooting for Dynamic Motion Retargeting
nodes.authors: Sergio A. Esteban, Jason H. K. Siu, Derrick Mach, Junheng Li, Vince Kurtz, Joel W. Burdick, Aaron D. Ames
nodes.summary: Motion retargeting approaches often prioritize kinematic similarity over whole-body dynamics, contact consistency, and actuation limits, yielding references that are difficult for reinforcement learning (RL) policies to reproduce, particularly for contact-rich behaviors. We present a contact-implicit, direct simulation-based multiple shooting (DSMS) framework that transforms kinematically feasible references into dynamically feasible whole-body trajectories. By embedding a differentiable simulator within a nonlinear program, DSMS resolves contact, friction, impacts, self-collision, and joint limits internally while enforcing tracking, actuation, and task constraints without prescribing a contact schedule or introducing explicit contact constraints. Compared with existing retargeting methods, DSMS accelerates motion-imitation RL training and yields policies with high success rates and low tracking error. We further demonstrate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on the Unitree G1 through command-conditioned walking, jogging, and contact-rich crawling, and a highly dynamic 180-degree jump-turn.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: TraceCAD: Trace-Guided Repair for Agentic CAD Generation
nodes.authors: Fengxiao Fan, Jingzhe Ni, Fan Sang, Xiaolong Yin, Yu Liu, Ruofeng Tong, Min Tang, Peng Du
nodes.summary: LLM-based CAD agents produce executable parametric programs, but their correction loops may lose evidence about satisfied requirements, faulty operations, and prior repairs. We introduce TraceCAD, a recovery layer that links requested features, modeling steps, failure evidence, and candidate outcomes as persistent state. TraceCAD diagnoses likely faulty operations, searches bounded edits in their dependency regions, validates candidates through execution and preservation checks, and retains successful and failed repair outcomes in reusable skill memory. On DeepCAD-derived benchmarks with 200-model ablations and a 1K-model comparison, TraceCAD achieves competitive geometric quality in terms of IoU, Chamfer distance, and Hausdorff distance. Removing persistent state nearly halves recovery score; removing localized search more than doubles geometric regression and doubles code-agent invocations. Initializing the skill store on disjoint training models further reduces retries, token cost, and latency. These results demonstrate that persistent, localized, and reusable recovery improves final CAD quality and repair reliability.
nodes.subject: Human Body

nodes.title: PFM-HR: Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots
nodes.authors: Yukang Gao, Yi Gu, Yangchen Zhou, Xingyu Chen, Zhaorui Wang, Fanghai Zhang, Hanyang Cao, Zhengyang Shen, Ji Ma, Runhan Zhang, Lei Han, Renjing Xu
nodes.summary: Motion priors improve reinforcement learning for physics-based humanoid tracking, but temporal priors require ordered motion clips, while pose priors provide limited guidance for policy-induced pose transitions. We present Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots (PFM-HR), a reusable flow matching prior trained directly on large scale unordered pose data. PFM-HR introduces the Pose Geometry Score (PGS), which quantifies how joint coordinate changes during rollouts align with the local geometry of pose variation captured by the prior. Using PGS to modulate the tracking reward guides policy exploration toward structured pose changes while keeping the prior frozen across tracking tasks. Experiments demonstrate that PFM-HR improves both single motion and general motion tracking, especially for highly dynamic motions.

nodes.title: Morphology-Aware Implicit Super-Resolution Network for Pathological Images
nodes.authors: Jiaming Liang, QiHui Han, Haolin Chen, Chengxin Ye, Jiawen Liu, Jiazhou Chen, Xiaoqi Sheng, Hongmin Cai
nodes.summary: Accurate diagnosis in Digital Pathology (DP) relies on high-resolution whole-slide images, yet clinical deployment is often limited by hardware costs. Super-Resolution (SR) offers a promising alternative by computationally enhancing low-resolution acquisitions. However, existing SR methods frequently struggle to preserve fine-grained cellular morphology, leading to texture oversmoothing and blurred structural boundaries under complex tissue variability. To address this issue, we propose Morph-ISR, a morphology-aware implicit super-resolution framework for DP that restores diagnostically relevant details with sub-pixel precision. Morph-ISR reformulates SR as a continuous coordinate-based reconstruction problem and integrates an Implicit Position-aware Kernel Generator (IPKG) to adaptively model spatially varying tissue morphology. To further enhance structural fidelity, a Morphological Fidelity Prior (MFP) is introduced, leveraging semantic guidance from a pre-trained cell segmentation network to enforce boundary-preserving and region-aware reconstruction, thereby improving the representation of critical cellular boundaries and nuclear textures. Experiments on TCGA and SurGen datasets show that Morph-ISR achieves the best LPIPS and ST-LPIPS among the evaluated methods, reducing them by up to 38.37% and 39.55%, respectively, over the second-best methods while maintaining strong PSNR and SSIM. These results demonstrate superior preservation of diagnostically relevant cellular boundaries and nuclear textures, while compact parameterization and high throughput support efficient edge deployment. Code and trained models will be released upon publication.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: An ECG foundation model for zero-shot transfer from hospital to point-of-care devices
nodes.authors: Edoardo Coppola, Stefano Fiorini, Pietro Liò, Mattia Savardi, Alberto Signoroni
nodes.summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) recording is moving from hospitals to point-of-care devices that record one or two leads, where public labelled data is too scarce to build foundation models (FMs) as for 12-lead ECGs. Whether existing 12-lead FMs transfer to these devices without retraining is unknown. We show that seven published FMs reach a zero-shot AUROC of 41-81% on two real point-of-care datasets and, when reduced to one or two leads, lose 12-35 AUROC points on average and gain 0.15-0.23 in mean absolute error across 29 benchmarks covering 1,673 clinical targets. We present RELAY, a 7-million-parameter FM that represents ECGs as graphs of segments from whichever leads are recorded, without filling missing ones or knowing their identities. Pretrained on 9.2 million 12-lead ECGs, RELAY is competitive with 12 leads, ranks first on both point-of-care datasets (AUROC 87.6% and 81.5%) and on 26 and 22 of 29 benchmarks with one and two random leads, and keeps the most informative operating point when 12-lead thresholds are applied to device recordings. Matched ablations show that omitting absent leads, rather than filling them, reduces what RELAY loses in transfer. ECG FMs should therefore be judged across all the acquisition settings, not on 12-lead benchmarks alone.
nodes.subject: Generative POI Search and Recommendation

nodes.title: Projection-Retraction MPPI: Exact Command-Space Constraint-Manifold Control for Manipulators
nodes.authors: Seulchan Lee, Leesai Park, Minhyeong Kang, Sanghyun Kim
nodes.summary: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is widely used in manipulation for its gradient-free, parallel handling of non-convex costs. Manipulation tasks, however, often impose constraints that hold throughout the motion: a closed kinematic chain that two grasping arms keep exactly, or joint limits and obstacle clearances that are never crossed. Standard MPPI handles such constraints only through the cost, as soft penalties that hold approximately and fail under a strong task cost. To address this, we propose Projection-Retraction MPPI (PR-MPPI), which enforces the constraints inside the sampled dynamics. At every rollout step, the sampled velocity is projected to satisfy both constraint types: the equality restricts it to a subspace, and each inequality to a half-space within that subspace, so inequality handling never breaks the equality. This projection, however, satisfies the constraints only to first order, and a finite step leaves a small drift off the equality. Therefore, we retract the returned command back onto the constraint, so that the commanded configuration satisfies the equality to numerical tolerance, independently of task weighting. We validate PR-MPPI on 14-DoF dual-arm systems. In simulation, the returned commands satisfy the closed-chain equality to numerical tolerance through a joint-limit stress test and randomized obstacle avoidance, while the measured trajectories retain the joint-limit and obstacle margins. On real hardware, the arms of a Unitree H1-2 humanoid reactively avoid a moving obstacle. Code and experiment videos are available at https://rcilab.khu.ac.kr/prmppi/.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Romanized Arabic Across Dialects: Views, Usage Patterns, and Linguistic Variation
nodes.authors: Amr Keleg, Ahmed Amine Ben Abdallah, Taha Yassine, Chadi Helwe, Imane Guellil, Nedjma Ousidhoum
nodes.summary: Arabizi refers to Arabic written in Latin script. Although previous studies have shown that the prevalence and usage of Arabizi vary by factors such as region and age group, most NLP research on Arabic texts treats it as a temporary phenomenon resulting from limited technological support for the Arabic script. In this work, we engage with Arabic speakers to collect insights on their perceptions and usage of Arabizi. We further examine writing norms among speakers of different dialects, focusing on Algerian, Egyptian, Lebanese, Moroccan, and Tunisian Arabic. To this end, we release two resources. First, we perform a character-level alignment of Arabic words to study inter- and intradialectal variation across these five dialects, based on words transliterated by the surveyed participants (VARabiziLex), finding systematic intradialectal regularity and interdialectal variation. Second, to study Arabic speakers' ability to identify this stylistic variation at the sentence level, we build VARabiziCues, a manually curated parallel corpus of sentences written in Arabic script alongside multiple Arabizi transliterations, collected from speakers of the same five dialects. Our study presents the largest human-centered, cross-dialectal study of Arabizi perceptions and practices to date.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Hard Constraints, Smooth Gradients: Learning Feasible Inventory Policies via Differentiable Projection
nodes.authors: Patrick Helm, Jan-Niklas Doerr, Joren Gijsbrechts, Stefan Minner
nodes.summary: Many operational problems are constrained sequential decision processes with combinatorial action spaces and interdependent constraints. Mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) handle such constraints flexibly but scale poorly in stochastic environments. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) promises scalable decision rules, but existing methods either penalize constraints rather than enforce them, or rely on feasibility mechanisms that break down once constraints interact. We bridge this gap by embedding a differentiable optimization module inside the policy: a neural network proposes continuous action targets, a quadratic program projects them onto the relaxed feasible set, and a dual-informed integer mapping restores integrality while preserving feasibility. Given a differentiable simulator, the policy trains end-to-end from sampled trajectories using pathwise gradients, while handling hard constraints with similar flexibility to MILPs. We show that our approach has bounded error relative to an exact integer projection and ensures the entire feasible action space is reachable. We apply the method to multi-echelon production-inventory planning under shared resource and material constraints. Our policy attains an average optimality gap of 1% on 3-item instances and consistently outperforms a rolling-horizon multi-stage stochastic program by at least 5.6% in 10-item networks. Compared to state-of-the-art echelon base-stock policies, savings reach 15.3% on 40-item instances. On an industry-scale case study with nonstationary demand from ASML, we reduce average cost by up to 1.8% relative to the best-known benchmark policy. The savings are largest where planning is hardest: in tightly capacitated systems with high demand variability. More broadly, we show that DRL can improve upon state-of-the-art baselines in sequential decision problems with hard constraints, which are widespread in practice.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
nodes.authors: Jiajun Liang, Yucheng Liao, Yukang Cao, Jiazhe Wei, Ken Li, Wende Tan, Jiankun Zhang, ZY Cui, Jingkang Yang, Liucheng Guo, Shiqi Yang, B. Yang, Caifeng Shan, Ziwei Liu, Chenyang Si
nodes.summary:
Language remains an outlier in generative modeling: while images, video, and audio are increasingly modeled in continuous latent spaces, text generation still relies predominantly on discrete tokens. Existing continuous language models either inherit embedding spaces not designed for joint generation and decoding, or compress autoencoded latents to ease diffusion, sacrificing token-level fidelity. Instead of simplifying the representation to suit the generative model, we preserve a high-capacity, decodable text latent and design the diffusion model to learn its distribution directly.
  We introduce AURORA-LM, a continuous-latent diffusion language model that separates the construction of a decodable text representation from the modeling of its distribution. A Query-based Encoder-Decoder organizes text into a high-capacity, prefix-aligned latent sequence, and a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer learns its distribution through flow matching, generating blocks left to right while denoising positions within each block in parallel. Because such a latent is harder for diffusion to model, AURORA-LM restricts only the noisy-input pathway while retaining the full clean-latent prediction target, accommodating full-width latents without reducing decoder-facing capacity. We further calibrate the noise-level distribution to the latent width, and introduce self-trajectory consistency to bridge independently sampled training noise and iterative denoising at inference.
  AURORA-LM achieves the strongest performance among evaluated continuous and diffusion-based language models on OpenWebText free generation and XSum summarization. Scaling to 1B parameters with about 1500 EFLOPs of total compute yields further gains, surpassing a larger publicly released latent-diffusion language model under a matched evaluation protocol. All experiments are conducted on Ascend NPUs.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: GeoCore-9B: Towards Geo-Aware Generative Foundation Models in Earth Observation
nodes.authors: Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim
nodes.summary: Existing generative models for earth observation (EO) predominantly rely on fine-tuning natural image priors, which limits their scalability and introduces perspective biases that conflict with geospatial constraints. To address this, we introduce GeoCore-9B, a 9-billion-parameter generative foundation model, which is the first of its scale to be trained from scratch exclusively on EO data. Unlike previous EO foundation models, GeoCore-9B is built upon a Flow Matching-based Diffusion Transformer (DiT) and natively conditions generation on text descriptions and continuous geospatial metadata, including ground sample distances, latitudes, and longitudes. To overcome the convergence and spatial disorientation challenges of training at this scale, we propose a Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss. This objective distills structural Earth surface priors (e.g., terrain and urban areas) from a frozen specialist teacher network, constraining the diffusion latent trajectory during training without adding inference overhead. Pre-trained on the global-scale Git-10M dataset, GeoCore-9B demonstrates strong downstream versatility. Beyond standard proxy generative tasks, we show that GeoCore-9B can be effectively adapted for practical EO applications, including highly challenging tasks such as cloud removal and SAR-to-optical cross-modal translation. Extensive evaluations confirm that GeoCore-9B establishes new state-of-the-art performance in both visual fidelity and geographic structural accuracy.
nodes.subject: End-to-End AD

nodes.title: Twig: Parallel and Memory-Efficient Tree Speculative Decoding for Hybrid-Attention LLMs
nodes.authors: Li Wang, Yi Su, Xiabao Wu, Chiran You, Yongchao Liu, Zhan Qiu, Juelu Zhang, Jiajun Zheng, Fangxin Liu, Jie Zhang, Chen Tian, Chengying Huan
nodes.summary: Emerging LLMs increasingly interleave full attention with recurrent linear attention to reduce long-context serving costs. Tree speculative decoding could further accelerate these hybrid models, but recurrent linear-attention layers carry parent-dependent states. Existing engines therefore verify proposal trees sequentially and snapshot the full state per node, causing latency and memory to grow with tree and batch sizes. We present Twig, a kernel--runtime co-design for tree speculative decoding of hybrid LLMs. Twig derives a tree-structured factorization of the linear-attention recurrence and realizes it with a resource-efficient GPU kernel that verifies all nodes in parallel, accelerating linear-attention tree verification by 3.4--7.7$\times$. It losslessly represents speculative state updates as token-level factors and reconstructs only the accepted state, reducing transient state memory by 82--99$\times$ and freeing GPU memory for KV caches. We integrate Twig into SGLang, a widely deployed production LLM serving engine, and further optimize its runtime through batch-wide verification budgeting. Across four models, two GPU platforms, and diverse datasets, Twig achieves up to $4.72\times$ the offline decode throughput of autoregressive decoding and up to $2.03\times$ that of the strongest tree-speculative baseline. Under online agent workloads, Twig reduces TTFT and TPOT by up to $67.6\%$ and $49.9\%$, respectively, over the strongest tree-speculative baseline.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: RADAR Perception for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance onboard small-scale Quadrotor UAVs
nodes.authors: Dnyandeep Mandaokar, Bernhard Rinner
nodes.summary: Fast dynamic obstacle avoidance (DOA) on uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) demands not only low-latency control and actuation but also reliable, long-range perception to detect obstacles and estimate their motion in time to maneuver. We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first mmWave RADAR-based perception-and-control system for fast onboard DOA. We derive and analyze latency and spatial bounds that relate sensing range, relative speed, and control delay, yielding sufficient conditions for successful avoidance. We further extend prior latency analyses to include the decision latency of the tracker and trigger to evaluate them per trial. Our computationally efficient system combines a lightweight interacting multiple models (IMM) tracker with a control-barrier functions (CBF) controller that directly outputs evasive accelerations. In 300 throw experiments spanning three object sizes and varying visibility (light and dark), it achieves mean position errors of at most 0.15 m, 0.93m, and 0.87m in the x, y, and z directions, with a similar spread in 90 experiments in smoke. An onboard implementation on a Raspberry Pi 4B demonstrates real-time feasibility with an end-to-end processing latency of approximately 14ms per RADAR frame and a system latency of 75ms from first detection to the avoidance command. The UAV successfully avoided obstacles in all 20 tethered indoor flights and all 39 untethered outdoor avoidance maneuvers across three ball sizes, during both hover and forward flights at up to 5m/s with measured closing speeds up to 14.6m/s.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Characterizing Treatment-Context Medication Evidence Across Clinic Notes and Structured EHR Medication History
nodes.authors: Mingyang Jiang, Congning Ni, Weixin Liu, Zhijun Yin
nodes.summary: Clinic notes may describe medication changes that are not reflected in structured electronic health record (EHR) medication history at the same encounter. Differences in terminology and documentation timing further complicate the interpretation of these discrepancies. We evaluated medication normalization in clinic notes and examined how semantic and temporal matching affected overlap with structured history. A note-grounded reference was constructed from large language model (LLM)-proposed mentions, deterministic canonical projection, and existing targeted correction records; random-audit records were summarized separately. On 5,360 reference mention rows from held-out patients, conditional canonical agreement increased from 81.25% with surface matching to 93.58% after lexical cleanup and curated aliases. Candidate-reference mention alignment was evaluated separately, yielding an F1 score of 0.6547. Across 27,552 reference rows, exact same-visit overlap was 16.71%. Overlap reached 90.22% when ingredient and broad-category matches were permitted at the same visit or within 30 days before or after the note. Incomplete mapping of note-derived labels contributed to residual nonoverlap in ontology-backed comparisons. Exact-label comparison captured only part of the related medication information across sources; broader matches do not establish equivalent medication use or treatment events.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Déjà Cue: Localizing States in Object Histories via Vocabulary-Relative Coordinates
nodes.authors: Haofan Cao, Zhichao You, Yunkai Yang, Liang Guo, Jie Wang, Chongshou Li
nodes.summary: Object tracking preserves identity through visual changes, but cannot tell when an object is whole, cut, or peeled. We study state-moment retrieval: locating when a tracked object exhibits each state in a supplied set of descriptions. However, absolute image--text similarity can favor shared object semantics, obscuring the distinctions needed to localize individual states. Our insight is that the alternatives themselves provide a reference for measuring state evidence. We introduce Déjà Cue, a training-free framework that centers description embeddings on a state-balanced vocabulary mean, producing query directions that compare each state against its alternatives. Using frozen vision--language encoders, Déjà Cue calibrates frame scores and retrieves intervals at multiple durations within contiguous visible runs. We construct MS-VOST by annotating 620 object histories with 2,465 states. With the encoder and temporal search fixed, Déjà Cue improves all three localization metrics over absolute scoring across eight encoder configurations, raising Top-1 temporal IoU by 0.42--1.14 percentage points. These gains persist across four text constructions, and candidate-ranking analysis shows that the vocabulary reference brings relevant intervals forward within the same search space. These results establish the supplied state vocabulary as an object-specific reference for localizing semantic states from frozen visual representations.
nodes.subject: Spatial Agents

nodes.title: CoNav-UAV: Cooperative Dual-Altitude Aerial Navigation via Stackelberg Learning
nodes.authors: Junru Song, Wenhao Zhang, Yang Yang, Xuekai Qiu, Feifei Wang, Weien Zhou, Tingsong Jiang, Ying Wen, Yang Li, Wen Yao
nodes.summary: Aerial search missions often require an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to locate a target from only a brief description of its appearance and surroundings, a task known as target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN). The task demands city-scale exploration and grounding as well as collision-free close-range approach, two interleaved processes that are difficult to reconcile within a single agent. Most existing methods adapt the ground VLN paradigm to a single UAV and rely on external assistance to compensate for its inefficiency. A recent attempt deploys two UAVs at complementary altitudes but still depends on privileged sensing and trains the two agents independently, precluding any mutual adaptation. We propose CoNav-UAV, which models the task as a Stackelberg game between a high-altitude leader and a low-altitude follower to capture their sequential decisions and asymmetric observations and utilities, with both agents using only onboard sensing. We introduce Iterative Stackelberg Learning, which tailors optimization to each agent's role: the leader's high-level vision-language reasoning builds on pretrained capabilities and is refined through memory-based in-context learning, while the follower's precise motion control is fine-tuned through DAgger-style expert distillation. Alternating the two updates lets each agent continually adapt to the other's evolving behavior. CoNav-UAV outperforms single- and dual-agent baselines across three high-fidelity urban scenes from the AerialVLN benchmark. It improves success rate by up to 30.8 points on the learning scene and by up to 9.0 points under cross-scene transfer, where the leader reuses its learned memory and the follower is adapted with 2.6-3.7 times less target-scene data. Extensive ablations confirm the contributions of key components and the benefit of mutual adaptation, with consistent gains across VLM backbones.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: MANGO-Grasp: Mahalanobis Fields over Geometry-Oriented 3D Gaussians for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping
nodes.authors: Heng Zhang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Mike Zheng Shou, Weisi Lin, Yan Wu
nodes.summary: Cross-embodiment dexterous grasping aims to synthesize stable grasps across heterogeneous multi-fingered hands with little or no embodiment-specific tuning. Existing interaction-centric methods achieve promising results, but their object representations often underrepresent local surface geometry, hand descriptors do not explicitly capture both morphology and kinematics, and hand-object interaction modeling is typically isotropic. We propose MANGO-Grasp, an anisotropic interaction framework that represents objects as geometry-oriented 3D Gaussian primitives to better preserve local surface geometry, and encodes hands into pretrained descriptors that capture both morphology and kinematics. Hand-object interaction is modeled using anisotropic Mahalanobis fields that reflect the directional nature of contact and guide a shared optimization for grasp realization across embodiments. On the CMAP and MultiGripperGrasp benchmarks, MANGO-Grasp outperforms the strongest seen-hand baseline by up to 8.24 percentage points in simulation. It also transfers zero-shot to the unseen SharpaWave hand, improving over the strongest zero-shot baseline by up to 16.57 percentage points, and achieves 86% success in real-world experiments. The code and additional materials are available at https://connor-zh.github.io/MANGO-Grasp/.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: ReBRAC-v2: The Return of the King
nodes.authors: Denis Tarasov, Robert K. Katzschmann
nodes.summary: Recent offline reinforcement learning methods increasingly rely on expressive generative policies and specialized value guidance. We ask how far systematic modernization of a conventional behavior-regularized actor-critic can go while preserving algorithmic simplicity. ReBRAC-v2 directly trains an exact-likelihood normalizing-flow actor with likelihood, MSE, and MAE behavior regularization, classification-based residual critics, staged optimization, and multi-sample inference. We develop one shared configuration through roughly 600 Bayesian proposals on six OGBench tasks, then adapt only two behavior-regularization coefficients using a 16-point grid for the main comparisons. Across ten common OGBench categories, ReBRAC-v2 averages 74.8 versus 52.3 for the next-best method and ranks first in eight categories. Without structural changes, it also obtains the strongest compared averages on D4RL AntMaze (90.2) and Adroit (33.6). Motivated by these results, we extend evaluation to all 235 state-based single-task problems across the 47 dataset variants in the original OGBench suite. To our knowledge, this is the first complete evaluation in this setting; no compared baseline reports results across the full suite. Per-task scores and configurations establish ReBRAC-v2 as a reference baseline for future work beyond the common task subset. The complete cloning objective retains the highest average after coefficient retuning of its alternatives, while further ablations characterize training, capacity, and inference choices. These results demonstrate the strength of systematic engineering within a minimalist offline RL foundation.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: BiCAA: Bidirectional Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Agent
nodes.authors: Yibin Huang, Bin Xu, Hailong Cao, Conghui Zhu
nodes.summary: By iteratively retrieving and integrating external evidence, multi-step search enables search-augmented agents to tackle complex question answering. However, vanilla GRPO assigns rewards based solely on final answers, providing limited guidance for intermediate search steps. To provide fine-grained process feedback, we evaluate the value of each search step: it should acquire evidence that advances problem solving while avoiding redundant retrieval. Building on these complementary criteria, we introduce BiCAA, which combines Forward Solvability Gain (FSG) and Subsequent Reasoning Gain (SRG) for bidirectional credit assignment. To reward progress in evidence acquisition, FSG quantifies changes in ground-truth answer likelihood after each interaction. SRG compares the subsequent action's likelihood with and without the current interaction to approximately measure its support for subsequent reasoning, using this support as a proxy signal for non-redundant search to encourage effective and efficient search. BiCAA calibrates local feedback through asymmetric fusion; for policy optimization, it integrates accumulated process rewards with terminal outcome supervision. Across seven open-domain QA benchmarks and two Qwen backbones, experiments show improvements in average F1, particularly on multi-hop tasks.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Dense Language Generation Made Simple: Deterministic, Randomized, and Multi-Order Algorithms
nodes.authors: Ziyi Cai, Shuangping Li, Yiheng Shen, Kangning Wang, Peng Zhang
nodes.summary:
Language generation in the limit is a theoretical framework for studying how a generator can learn to produce new valid strings from a stream of positive examples. In this model, an adversary chooses an unknown language from a countable family and enumerates its elements in an arbitrary order, while the generator must eventually output only elements of the language that have not yet appeared in the enumeration. Reliable generation is thus formalized through two eventual guarantees: validity and novelty relative to the observed data. To further quantify the breadth of the generator's outputs, Kleinberg and Wei (FOCS 2025, STOC 2026) introduced lower density as a measure of output coverage. Given an order representing the importance or relevance of possible outputs, lower density is the asymptotic lower bound, as $n$ grows, on the fraction of the first $n$ elements of the target language that the generator outputs before they appear in the data. Kleinberg and Wei showed that $1/2$ is the optimal lower-density guarantee for deterministic algorithms.
  We develop a simple and unified framework for obtaining optimal lower-density guarantees. We first give a deterministic algorithm that recovers the optimal guarantee of $1/2$ with a significantly simpler analysis than prior work. We then demonstrate the flexibility of our framework through two extensions. First, against an oblivious adversary, randomization raises the optimal guarantee to $1-1/e$. Second, for any finite collection of orders, the optimal deterministic and randomized guarantees can be achieved simultaneously with respect to every order, so accommodating multiple notions of importance or relevance entails no loss in the optimal guarantee.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Gaokerena: A Small Persian Medical Language Model Family
nodes.authors: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Hamidreza Baradaran Kashani, Pedram Rostami, Sadra Hakim, Zahra Kazemi, Amirhossein Poursina, Milad Tavakoli, Audrina Ebrahimi
nodes.summary: Persian medical natural language processing remains limited by the scarcity of domain-specific resources and insufficient public characterization of their coverage and quality. We present Gaokerena, an openly released suite of Persian medical resources comprising an 85.5-million-word corpus of 101,954 web articles; MF3QA, a 24,000-pair patient-doctor question-answering dataset; 1,878 Iranian medical examination questions (KOPP); 1,089 manually translated medical MMLU questions (FA_MED_MMLU); and approximately 18,000 machine-translated MedMCQA training items filtered by two language-model evaluators. We characterize the resources' composition, orthographic variation, redundancy, topical coverage, privacy indicators, answer-key balance, extraction artefacts, and translation limitations. As application case studies, we adapt Aya-Expanse-8B into Gaokerena-V, trained on the corpus and MF3QA, and Gaokerena-R, developed through preference-based reasoning distillation. On translated medical MMLU, Gaokerena-V achieves 49.31% accuracy under direct prompting, compared with 46.65% for Aya-Expanse-8B; the paired exact McNemar test is statistically inconclusive (p = 0.0502). Gaokerena-R reaches 52.80% using five-sample self-consistency and a verifier, but this higher-compute setting is not directly comparable. Under matched five-sample chain-of-thought self-consistency without a verifier, Gaokerena-R scores 48.58%, versus 46.92% for Aya-Expanse-8B, a non-significant difference (p = 0.190). English evaluation also reveals a substantial performance gap relative to Persian. To our knowledge, Gaokerena provides the first openly released and systematically characterized suite of Persian medical resources alongside generative models built on them. These protocol-specific results do not establish an isolated training advantage or clinical readiness.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: UDT: Reconciling U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers with Data-Adaptive Token Reduction
nodes.authors: Junno Yun, Yaşar Utku Alçalar, Mehmet Akçakaya
nodes.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as a core architecture in generative modeling due to their scalability and adaptability to multimodal tasks. DiTs comprise isotropic transformer blocks, and learn representations progressively across depth, where the denoising objective drives later layers to focus on fine-detail reconstruction. This results in degraded representation quality and an imbalanced encoder-decoder behavior. Prior approaches such as representation alignment (REPA) mitigate this by encouraging stronger early representations via training regularization. Alternatively, U-Net-style DiT architectures introduce explicit multi-scale encoder-decoder structures for improved convergence. But they build on standard U-Net wisdom via learnable operators for spatial downsampling, which are not well-suited to transformer architectures, introducing inefficiencies and compatibility issues with components such as cross-attention and representation regularization. In this work, we propose UDT, a U-Net diffusion transformer that combines the representation power of DiTs with the encoding-decoding benefits of U-Nets, through data-adaptive token merging for downsampling and upsampling, while preserving the DiT token dimension. Our baseline UDT architecture outperforms existing U-Net DiTs and achieves performance comparable to REPA across all model sizes. Furthermore, using architectural optimization and REPA, UDT outperforms SiT's 7.9 FID at 1400 epochs (w/o CFG) within 40 epochs (~ 40x faster convergence) for XL model size on 256x256 ImageNet. Finally, it achieves strong image generation performance with CFG, reaching FID of 1.38 (320 epochs) with SD-VAE and 1.35 (500 epochs) with VA-VAE, providing a new backbone for DiTs with strong empirical benefits. Code is available at https://github.com/JN-Yun/UDT
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: You Don't Need To Stay in The Loop: An Agentic Robotics Loop for Robot-Policy Improvement
nodes.authors: Hang Yu
nodes.summary: Coding agents close the software loop for training a robot policy without having a human in the loop: a main agent manages the training, subagents analyze and execute, treat robot policies and hardware as tools and do the work. We port this architecture to robot-policy improvement, where one difference dominates the design: robotic tools such as trained policies, training pipelines, and data collection fail routinely, so a tool's quality must be measured, recorded at every call, and expired when the artifact behind it changes. AgenticRobotics is a backend-independent control plane in which an LLM controller drives disposable workers through durable train--evaluate--improve transactions: an immutable objective, controller-owned measurement, commit-keyed crash recovery, an evidence-graded skill library, and a tool registry with a standardized, recorded call surface. The title is an operational claim, not a selection claim: the operator can leave because promotion is evidence-gated, state is recoverable, and capability quality is derived from records, not because the loop picks better checkpoints than a human. On the one lineage we measured, it does not. The gates provide measured false-promotion control (0.001 false promotions per run with the hardened margin, against 0.005--0.021 with the shipped rule), anytime-valid decisions under optional stopping, zero lost or duplicate effects under kill injection, and a signed verifier that caught six of six artifact-tampering classes.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Tevatron Meets Megatron: Expert-Parallel LLM Reranker Training on an Academic Budget
nodes.authors: Zhichao Xu, Xueguang Ma, Shengyao Zhuang, Luyu Gao, Wenqian Ye, Yu Wang, Jamie Callan, Jimmy Lin
nodes.summary: Training large dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) rerankers is constrained by GPU memory and distributed-execution efficiency, which has kept academic reranker research largely on dense models. Tevatron trains rerankers through the Hugging Face Trainer with DeepSpeed and PyTorch FSDP1, a stack that stalls on three fronts: DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 has a known gradient-gathering failure on this path, FSDP1 full sharding is memory-safe but throughput-bound, and neither offers the expert parallelism (EP) that MoE training needs. We present Tevatron 3.0, which integrates Megatron-Core as a reranker training backend while preserving Tevatron's data processing, evaluation pipeline, and Hugging Face checkpoint format. For full-parameter dense 8B training, Megatron matches FSDP1 on BEIR-15 NDCG@10 with approximately 4% lower epoch time and twice the peak GPU memory under matched data-parallel and recomputation settings, and approximately 22% lower epoch time in its recommended configuration; it supports both LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning. Expert parallelism makes it possible to train a 30B-parameter MoE reranker (Qwen3-30B-A3B) on two nodes. A controlled study of architecture, LoRA, and distillation on BEIR-15, with three first-stage retrievers and Hugging Face and vLLM serving, shows that the MoE reranker matches dense-8B quality at less than half the activated parameters and at higher inference throughput. We open-source the framework and trained checkpoints.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: Gaokerena: A Small Persian Medical Language Model Family
nodes.authors: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Hamidreza Baradaran Kashani, Pedram Rostami, Sadra Hakim, Zahra Kazemi, Amirhossein Poursina, Milad Tavakoli, Audrina Ebrahimi
nodes.summary: Persian medical natural language processing remains limited by the scarcity of domain-specific resources and insufficient public characterization of their coverage and quality. We present Gaokerena, an openly released suite of Persian medical resources comprising an 85.5-million-word corpus of 101,954 web articles; MF3QA, a 24,000-pair patient-doctor question-answering dataset; 1,878 Iranian medical examination questions (KOPP); 1,089 manually translated medical MMLU questions (FA_MED_MMLU); and approximately 18,000 machine-translated MedMCQA training items filtered by two language-model evaluators. We characterize the resources' composition, orthographic variation, redundancy, topical coverage, privacy indicators, answer-key balance, extraction artefacts, and translation limitations. As application case studies, we adapt Aya-Expanse-8B into Gaokerena-V, trained on the corpus and MF3QA, and Gaokerena-R, developed through preference-based reasoning distillation. On translated medical MMLU, Gaokerena-V achieves 49.31% accuracy under direct prompting, compared with 46.65% for Aya-Expanse-8B; the paired exact McNemar test is statistically inconclusive (p = 0.0502). Gaokerena-R reaches 52.80% using five-sample self-consistency and a verifier, but this higher-compute setting is not directly comparable. Under matched five-sample chain-of-thought self-consistency without a verifier, Gaokerena-R scores 48.58%, versus 46.92% for Aya-Expanse-8B, a non-significant difference (p = 0.190). English evaluation also reveals a substantial performance gap relative to Persian. To our knowledge, Gaokerena provides the first openly released and systematically characterized suite of Persian medical resources alongside generative models built on them. These protocol-specific results do not establish an isolated training advantage or clinical readiness.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Measurement Without Validity: The Compounding Reliability Problem in Agentic AI Evaluation
nodes.authors: William Caban
nodes.summary:
Agentic AI evaluation pipelines produce benchmark scores that justify deployment decisions, safety certifications, and regulatory compliance claims. No formal framework has characterized how validity degrades across these stages.
